observations: Both photos show a large pile of multiple used green corded power drills stacked together, not a single isolated item.
The word 'BOSCH' is legible in white text on at least one tool body in photo 1.
Cords, chucks and nameplates are mostly obscured by overlapping tools; no voltage or chuck-size markings are legible in either photo.
No plug, power cable end, or rating plate is clearly visible in either photo.
Tools appear worn, dusty, and used (second-hand bulk stock), consistent with a 'tokunbo' resale shop.

claims.evidence: No voltage rating plate or plug visible in either photo.
No chuck or nameplate clearly visible in either photo to confirm size.
Brand text 'BOSCH' legible on a tool in photo 1.

risks.risk: Specific unit buyer receives is unclear since photos show a mixed pile, not the individual item for sale.
risks.proof: A photo of the single actual unit being sold, isolated and clearly labeled.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic used unit, lowest condition in the pile

risks.risk: Working condition unknown; used tools in bulk piles are often untested or faulty.
risks.proof: Video of the drill powering on and spinning under load.

risks.risk: Chuck size (claimed 13mm) unverified, affects capability and price tier.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of chuck or nameplate showing size.
risks.if_unproven: priced as smallest common chuck size (10mm) until proven

risks.risk: Voltage (claimed 220v) unverified; some used imports are 110v needing a converter.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of rating plate or plug.
risks.if_unproven: priced as needing voltage verification, treated as uncertain/non-standard

risks.risk: Cord and internal wiring condition unknown; visible coiled cords could be damaged or repaired with tape/splices.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of full cord length and plug.

proof_requests: Photo of the single exact unit being sold, separated from the pile.
Close-up of the nameplate showing voltage, wattage, and model number.
Close-up of the chuck showing size markings.
Video of the drill powering on and chuck spinning.
response.reason: A Bosch-branded used corded drill is identifiable by type and brand from photo 1, but with no visible nameplate, chuck, or power-on proof, it must be priced at worst case as an untested generic used unit with unverified voltage and chuck size.
